summary.prose: Restore the catalog-backed Tracker section in the registered-repo panel and attach the existing approval prompter to the VS Code extension lifecycle. One panel selection targets one registered repository. One activation owns one subscription, and the daemon broker owns request lifetime and arbitration. The remaining work repairs test fixtures and assertions against current contracts.

api.name: createApprovalPrompter
api.signature: createApprovalPrompter(opts: { client: IpcClient; notifier: ApprovalNotifier; reconnectMs?: number }): ApprovalPrompter

parameters.name: opts
parameters.purpose: Supply active daemon client and native VS Code notification adapter

returns.meaning: Existing start, stop, and open lifecycle

errors.condition: Use existing stale-answer or transport handling without inventing a decision

preconditions: Extension owns one prompter for the attached client
postconditions: Start once at activation and stop on disposal. Reconnect through existing prompter

Show the daemon's redacted gate content [c2] [c6]. Approve and Decline answer only a currently open request. Show details opens approvalDetails(request) as JSON and offers the same choices again after the JSON opens, if still active. The notifier keeps the same pending choice and handle throughout. Dismissal resolves undefined. The close hook invalidates the handle and prevents reopening or answering after cancel, stream loss or extension disposal, even if VS Code still displays the old toast. The daemon owns expiry and first accepted answer.

alternativesConsidered.name: Restore the existing editor contracts
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Restore the two missing VS Code integrations using the daemon contracts and fix drifted coverage.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Use the existing config catalog and repo-settings gateway for Tracker rows and the existing approval subscriber for daemon prompts. Keep current wire and storage contracts. Update the tests for current fixture names, taxonomy, settings activation, and registry membership.
pros: Recovers documented editor approval behavior and existing Tracker functionality.
Keeps authorization, state ownership and validation with the daemon.
cons: Requires integration tests for editor attachment, repo changes and stale messages.

alternativesConsidered.name: Retire the missing editor surfaces
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Treat the missing Tracker controls and approval prompt as product removals.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Define the current VS Code panel as model and provider configuration only and delegate tool approvals and Tracker configuration to other existing clients. Align client tests and documented support with those narrower contracts.
pros: Leaves the currently active editor surfaces smaller.
cons: Conflicts with the current documented editor approval behavior and leaves users without the two editor surfaces.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: It can refresh assertions, but would remove existing user-facing coverage without product evidence that those editor capabilities were retired.

participants.label: VS Code extension

participants.label: Approval prompter
participants.description: Owns notification handles and the existing streaming client.

participants.label: Daemon approval broker
participants.description: Owns decisions, cancellation and request expiration.

participants.label: VS Code notification
participants.description: Shows redacted data and presents the user's choices.

messages.label: Start after daemon client is ready
messages.description: One subscriber belongs to the extension activation.

messages.label: Gate frame
messages.description: Supply the redacted request and request ID.

messages.label: Show Approve, Decline, Show details
messages.description: Display a native notification for each open request ID.

messages.label: Choose Show details, answer, or dismiss
messages.description: Show details keeps the notification handle and final decision promise pending. Dismissal leaves the daemon decision pending.

messages.label: Open redacted JSON and ask again if active
messages.description: Open approvalDetails(request) as JSON, then offer the same choices if the request handle is still active. Cancel, disconnect, and disposal invalidate the handle even if the JSON or toast stays visible.

messages.label: Answer if still open
messages.description: Send the request ID and decision through approval.answer.

messages.label: Accepted or stale result
messages.description: Honor the broker response and surface stale answers.

messages.label: Cancel or end stream
messages.description: Invalidate notification handles. Reconnect on stream loss while active.

messages.label: Stop on disposal
messages.description: End subscription and invalidate outstanding notifications.
